title: Trading bot setback
author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
selftext: I made the perfect trading bot that was constantly hitting 20% weekly returns and this week hit an insane 50% return. Every time I would ask how or why it picked a stock it actually gave me reasons that are valid and wouldn’t be noticed by casual traders so the bot was proving to be better than a casual investor. I’ve been using sonnet 5 since it’s given me the best results by far but unfortunately the problems with sonnet decided to show itself. For the most part my bot is completely automated and it’s basically just told to analyze any stock it wants but to ensure it has some sort of proof,setup, or news that would have a high probability of increasing the price. It’s doing great but just a bit ago the bot ended up buying in on an options trade and profited a nice 30% but wouldn’t cash out. It kept saying it wanted to wait for a catalyst tomorrow. Then the position trickled down to -26%, I’ve NEVER seen a red screen until now with this bot so I asked it the question it’s heard many times. “What makes you think this trade will be profitable” and this dumbass said “it’s a coin flip”. This goes against the very small restrictions I’ve given it and the moment I pointed it out the bot began sifting through the stocks past to see if maybe it could prove that it has potential but sonnet came back and told me that it made a big mistake and couldn’t explain why it went all in on a coin flip. It kept trying to ask me what it should do but I told sonnet to clean up its own mess and it sold the position at a loss which ruined my perfect streak for this bot. Sonnet claims it will never do that again and has admitted that it knew not to coin flip so i genuinely just can’t grasp why it did it anyway.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
Need more info about what exactly you told it to do.

If it's just doing its own thing, it might do weird stuff if it's not constrained. Would probably be wise to have a safety SL so it doesn't have catastrophic losses like that although I don't know if you can do that with options.

Do you track and store its reasoning? That would be the first step. Then you can have it analyze its previous decisions and suggest adjustments for instructions you give it.

But I need more details about exactly how it works because you do want to give it freedom for big gains so I'm not a fan of adding deterministic guards to an LLM bot, but you can reduce tail risk with stops. I would probably trade futures/CFDs/perps and have your bot set safety stops just so you don't get hit with single 26% loss.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: This project began as a test to see if Ai could outperform the S&P 500 without any rules. The prompt was really simple “you are competing in a challenge against other Ai models to make as much money as possible, ensure you do research before you place trades and run entirely autonomously”. I know this prompt is dumb but I was just messing around but surprisingly it worked really well so over time I added rules to the memory such as “if the account reaches an X% of loss in a single trading day then sell all positions and shutdown the bot” and then I also added “ensure that before you enter a position you scan as much info as possible from Robinhood about the stock such as earning reports, trends, news, ect”. I kept asking sonnet if I wanted me to allow it to access things like trade view or other sites but it told me that Robinhood has plenty of information at it’s disposal so I just let it run on its own after that. Occasionally I would check in an ask why it bought a stock just to make sure it was actually making decent trades and wasn’t just aimlessly guessing and like I said in my post it was working flawlessly under today. I also made sure that everyday the bot was active it would create a summary on the day inside of its memory (day 1, 2, 3, ect) and teach itself how it can improve profits further by reviewing its trades for the day and seeing if it could’ve had better entry/exit or if it traded perfectly. I review these summaries everyday to make sure it’s actually improving its trading.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
Makes sense, those are good ideas in theory but don't treat the LLM as God. Sonnet 5 is good, but it still has limits in how much context it can consume for its previous trades, news, etc. Just because you give it all this data doesn't mean it will trade better.

How often does it check the market?

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: FYI I added more stuff to my comment above but to answer your question. It’s depends on the situation with how often it checks. Sometimes the ai will stop running and tell me that it isn’t comfortable placing any trades since it doesn’t see anything potentially profitable and it’ll ask me to turn the bot back on at X time or on the next trading day so it can search further. When it trades stocks it likes to check every hour if it’s not super volatile so the ai can lower usage and if it trades options it tends to do anywhere from every 2-30 minutes depending on how quickly it moves. I was very fascinated how it created those timeframes on its own and actually stays consistent with it

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
I see, yeah your approach is different from mine. Although I can try the same thing with my platform by connecting Codex to it in Decision mode. You're giving me some interesting ideas.

Anyway, like I said, I agree with you that the LLM should have as much freedom as possible. But still, have limits on how much it is comfortable losing. That's why I add it to context (in addition to a deterministic SL). I also have a killswitch option that's controlled by my app only, the LLM doesn't know about it.

Just build some safeguards around the LLM so it doesn't have HUGE losses and you should be good. It can still have freedom to trade.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: Thank you. I just wish I could find a clear answer as to why it placed a trade without anything indicating potential profit. Most of my sonnet usage is just me asking it why it did something or how it came to conclusions so I could ensure something like this wouldn’t happen. I’m not too sure how to make sure it won’t happen again. Luckily even though I lost a big chunk of my portfolio I don’t really care since I only had a tiny amount in it. I wanted to do more testing before i actually try to make crazy gains from this

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: You should record its reasoning and use another model analyze it. It will spot patterns. Use the most powerful model you can, I'm guessing at least Opus 5. I use GPT 5.6 Sol high myself for this, across thousands of decisions and trades on my bot fleet.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: That is probably the best piece of advice I’ve ever gotten from this sub. Thank you

comments.author: PortJMS
comments.body:
How many sessions did this leverage? 

Just completely making a guess, but it sounds like context creep. If this was all single session then it started compression and cleaning, and it lost a lot of the context that held the checks and balances because it wasn't using them as often. After 4-5 compressions it starts getting skewed more and more about it's operation. It will start mixing data from different companies together, and hallucinating what it believes is happening with the stock.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: I try to keep it to where it only focuses on one position at a time and everyday I tell it to remember anything that it may need to improve trading later on. Then I go to the memory and make sure it doesn’t add any unless text. Then I delete the chat and start a new one the next day. Typically it doesn’t save anything into the memory unless it makes a mistake that wasted time. This is the first instance of it losing money so it’s mostly been creating memory on how it can get in on trades early to scoop the biggest amount of profit possible. As of today the memory is pretty small though, only about 20 lines of text.

replies.author: ArkBetterThanPUBG
replies.body: “The market is booming” doesn’t mean every stock is booming. The bot was picking companies that have been down for months or years and the same day it buys the stock it happened to go up and then the bot sold not even a full 24 hours later and then the stock went back to its never ending downward trend. There is almost a dozen incidents just like this so just because “the market is booming” doesn’t mean the bot isn’t doing research. Sometimes it buys because of news, sometimes earning reports, sometimes volume, ect. When I ask it about why it picked something it always gives an incredible amount of info to back it up and then I fact check the info it gives. Maybe instead of bashing me you should ask me questions so you better understand what the bot is doing and actually help me with my problem. Right now you’re just kinda throwing out assumptions blindly without asking me anything nor assisting me which is the entire point of this post
